questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 1 in this lesson produce?

person = {'name': 'Aylin', 'age': 20}
print(person.get('name'))
person['age'] += 1
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`person = {'name': 'Aylin', 'age': 20}` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`print(person.get('name'))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`person['age'] += 1` — Updates an existing result; without it, a counter or total stays unchanged.

`student = {'name': 'Aylin', 'score': 95}` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`print(student['name'], student.get('grade', 'not set'))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`prices = {'tea': 3, 'bread': 2}` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`for item, price in prices.items():` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`print(item, price)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
